- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon (first 5–10 days).
- Forecast tends to peak too early and then overcorrects, leading to overshoots followed by sharp declines.
- Mean reversion is underemphasized; model fails to account for price stabilization after spikes.
- Lagged corrections are missing — model doesn’t adjust for recent true price movements in the forecast.
- High volatility in true outcomes is not captured; model underestimates magnitude of price swings.
- Forecast assumes linear continuation of recent trends, ignoring structural breaks or policy shocks.
- Model overreacts to short-term noise, especially in the first 5–7 days of the forecast.
- Price spikes are forecasted too aggressively, leading to overestimation of peak values.
- Model underestimates the persistence of upward trends after initial spikes.
- Forecast horizon is too optimistic — model fails to account for delayed market reactions.
